overview: Two forms the same protozoan takes — one built for feeding and moving, the other built for surviving the outside world.
genZNote: The active troublemaker versus the one just waiting it out.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The active, motile, feeding form of a protozoan parasite found in the host or in fresh, warm specimens.
aspects.valueB: The dormant, resistant, non-feeding form that allows the parasite to survive outside the host and transmit to a new one.

aspects.label: Motility
aspects.valueA: Motile, using pseudopods, flagella, or cilia depending on the organism.

aspects.label: Metabolic Activity
aspects.valueA: Metabolically active — feeds, replicates (by binary fission).
aspects.valueB: Metabolically dormant; a protective wall halts activity.

aspects.label: Environmental Resistance
aspects.valueA: Fragile — quickly destroyed outside the host (e.g. by stomach acid, drying).
aspects.valueB: Resistant to gastric acid, desiccation, and chlorination, enabling fecal-oral transmission.

aspects.label: Infective vs Diagnostic Stage
aspects.valueA: Usually the diagnostic stage found in acute/dysenteric stool, but not typically the infective stage.
aspects.valueB: Typically the infective stage ingested by a new host, and also a key diagnostic stage in formed stool.

aspects.label: Example Organism
aspects.valueA: Entamoeba histolytica trophozoite, seen in acute amebic dysentery.
aspects.valueB: Entamoeba histolytica cyst, seen in chronic or asymptomatic carriage and responsible for transmission.
